preconditions.description: The input is a single integer k where 1 ≤ k ≤ 10^9.

postconditions.expression: all(line.strip() in ['N', 'Y'] * n for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) and all(line == line[::-1] for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) and all(line[i] == 'N' for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] for i in range(n) if i == 0) and any('Y' in line for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The output is a valid undirected adjacency matrix of size n×n (2 ≤ n ≤ 1000) with 'N' or 'Y' entries, where Gii = 'N' and Gij = Gji for all i, j.

postconditions.expression: n == int(stdout.splitlines()[0].strip()) and n >= 2 and n <= 1000
postconditions.description: The first line of the output is an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 1000) representing the number of vertices.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.splitlines()) == n + 1 and all(len(line.strip()) == n for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The adjacency matrix has exactly n rows and n columns.

postconditions.expression: any('Y' in line for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) and any('Y' in stdout.splitlines()[1][i] for i in range(n)) and any('Y' in stdout.splitlines()[-1][i] for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: There exists at least one path between vertex 1 and vertex 2 (i.e., there is at least one 'Y' in row 1 and column 2, and vice versa, and connectivity is guaranteed).

The number of shortest paths between vertex 1 and vertex 2 in the constructed graph is exactly k, where count_shortest_paths(k_str, graph_str) is a helper function that computes the number of shortest paths in the given graph (defined as the number of distinct paths of minimal length between vertex 1 and vertex 2).
